title: Pretty good shadow tomography
authors: Sabee Grewal, Angelos Pelecanos, Jack Spilecki, Ewin Tang, John Wright
abstract: We give a shadow tomography algorithm that uses $O(\log(m) \log(m/δ) / \varepsilon^2)$ copies of the input state. Specifically, given a quantum state $ρ$ and observables $O_1,\ldots,O_m$, the algorithm outputs estimates of $\mathrm{tr}(O_iρ)$ for all $i\in[m]$ that are all accurate to within $\pm\varepsilon$, except with probability at most $δ$. The key idea is to work in the average-case setting: for a random state drawn from a known prior, a pretty good measurement on $O(\log(m)/\varepsilon^2)$ copies gives a constant-error guarantee on all but a small fraction of the prior. Boosting this guarantee gives an average-case shadow tomography algorithm, and the minimax principle then (non-constructively) implies the existence of a measurement with the same worst-case guarantee.   We also identify an obstruction to further improvement with this approach. While pretty good measurements amplify success over the randomness of the prior, they do not amplify success over the randomness of measurement. This issue appears to be inherent, and gives rise to the remaining $\log(m)$ factor separating the complexity of the quantum problem from its classical counterpart.
summary: This paper presents an efficient, dimension-free algorithm for shadow tomography, estimating many expectation values of an unknown quantum state. It achieves a complexity scaling of $O(\log(m) \log(m/\delta)/\epsilon^2)$ copies. The method cleverly uses the average-case setting combined with the minimax theorem to establish a strong worst-case guarantee.
main_problem: The paper addresses shadow tomography: estimating the expectation values of a large set of observables $\{O_1, \dots, O_m\}$ for an unknown quantum state $ho$ using multiple copies of $ho$.
main_result: They derive an algorithm requiring $O(\log(m) \log(m/\delta)/\epsilon^2)$ copies to estimate all expectation values within $\pm\epsilon$ with high probability.
method: The approach leverages the average-case setting, utilizing Pretty Good Measurements (PGM) and applying Sion's minimax theorem to lift the average-case guarantee to a worst-case guarantee.
model_or_system: The system involves an unknown quantum state $ho$ and a set of $m$ observables $\{O_i\}$. The analysis is general, focusing on the complexity scaling with the number of observables $m$.
key_observables: The expectation values $	ext{tr}(O_iho)$ for $i \in [m]$.
important_parameters: The complexity scales with $m$ (number of observables), $\epsilon$ (accuracy), and $\delta$ (failure probability).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the average-case formulation and the non-constructive implication from the minimax theorem. A key limitation is the remaining $\log(m)$ factor separating the quantum problem from its classical one.
paper_structure: The paper develops the algorithm by first establishing bounds in the average-case setting, then using the minimax principle to claim the worst-case bound. It concludes by identifying inherent limitations in the approach.
why_interesting: This work provides state-of-the-art complexity bounds for quantum state characterization, which is fundamental for quantum characterization protocols in quantum computing and quantum sensing.
